ownerThemes.theme: PatternReview members comparing the 4423, 4432 and 4452 describe them as the same machine with different stitch counts and accessory packs, and suggest buying on price.
Comparison sites and forum posters call the 4432 the value pick of the line: 32 stitches for about $26 more than the 4423, and the same head as the 4452 without the accessory pack.
The bobbin, tension and skipped-stitch complaints documented for the 4423 apply to the shared 44-series head.

crossShop.why: Same head with nine fewer stitches, usually a little cheaper.
Same head with a walking foot, nonstick foot and clearance plate added.
Buyers who want fewer stitches but a quieter, more adjustable mechanical.

editorial.verdict: The middle Singer Heavy Duty: the 4423's head with 32 stitches, and the 4452's head without the accessory pack.
editorial.whoFor: Beginners who want more stretch and decorative stitches than the 4423 and do not need the 4452's walking foot right away.
editorial.skipIf: You already know you want a walking foot, in which case the 4452 pack is usually cheaper than buying one separately.
strengths: Singer lists 1,100 spm and a metal interior frame.
32 stitches cover stretch and decorative work the 4423 lacks.
Class 15 bobbins and snap-on feet are cheap and everywhere.
weaknesses: Machine weight and dimensions were not published in accessible sources.
Four basic feet in the box; no walking or nonstick foot.
Shares the 44-series bobbin and tension complaints.

checks.title: Price it against the 4452
checks.body: If the 4452 is within $20 to $30, its walking foot and nonstick foot alone cover the difference.

checks.title: Color and edition listings
checks.body: Singer sells black and special edition 4432 variants at different prices. Confirm the stitch count is 32 and the head is the same before paying for a color.

checks.title: Confirm weight for portability
checks.body: Some listings show 17.4 lb, which appears to be shipping weight. Ask the dealer for machine weight if you carry it to class.
